newsitem.title: JAPAN: Refineries, power plants unaffected by oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Refineries, power plants unaffected by oil spill.

text.p: Operations of oil refineries and nuclear power plants have not been affected by an oil spill from a sunken Russian tanker in the Sea of Japan, company spokesmen said on Tuesday.

"Our power plant is running as usual and the oil slicks are no longer likely to affect the operations as they seem to be drifting up north away from the plant area," a spokesman for the Japan Atomic Power Co said.
The firm operates two nuclear reactors, with a total capacity of 1.5 million kilowatts, in the coastal city of Tsuruga in Fukui Prefecture.
The Russian-registered Nakhodka, carrying 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, broke in two during storms last Thursday.

The bow section of the ship, believed to contain 2,800 tonnes of oil, and some slicks were spotted 4.4 km north of Anto Point in Fukui prefecture, about 80 km north of the Japan Atomic Power's plant site, at 11.15 a.m. (0215 GMT), a Maritime Safety Agency official said.

Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said the oil slicks were unlikely to affect operations at its 11 nuclear reactors in the prefecture as the plants suck in seawater for cooling purposes from four to seven metres below the surface.
Kansai Electric's nuclear plants are located 80 to 90 km south of the area where the bow section was spotted.
The agency official said the bow section and some oil slicks around it were drifting eastwards, away from the plants.

Nihonkai Oil Co Ltd said the impact of the oil slicks on the firm's 60,000 barrel-per-day Toyama plant on the Sea of Japan coast would be minimal, as the refinery takes water for industrial use from nearby rivers.

The oil spills will not cause any serious problems in Nihonkai's unloading of crude as the slicks, which have constantly been drifting, are unlikely to stay around the firm's crude discharge area even if they reach there, a company spokesman said.
Nihonkai Oil has crude discharge buoys three km off the coast.

The refinery is about 125 km northeast of where the bow section and the slicks have been spotted, but is sheltered from them by the Noto Peninsula. The other refineries on the Sea of Japan coast, Nippon Oil Co Ltd's 26,000 bpd Niigata plant and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK's 40,000 bpd Niigata refinery, are more than 320 km away from the oil slicks.
Refineries are concentrated on the other side of Japan, the Pacific coast.
